## What managing Old Town takes.

### The Old Town Triangle
Crilly Court and the frame cottages and rowhouses of the Old Town Triangle sit in one of Chicago's oldest landmark districts, where exterior projects need landmark sign-off. We have the approval path down to a routine.

### Small buildings, big expectations
Most Old Town associations are 4-to-24-unit vintage buildings off Wells Street, exactly the size where self-management burns out volunteers and national firms under-serve. Our model was built for them.

### Wells Street mixed-use
Condos above the Wells Street corridor's restaurants and shops deal with shared systems, commercial neighbors, and nightlife hours. We keep the residential floors quiet, clean, and fairly billed.

## Old Town boards ask us first.

### Our Old Town building is in a landmark district, how does that affect projects?
Exterior work in the Old Town Triangle District generally requires review by the Commission on Chicago Landmarks before permits issue. We build that review into project timelines, prepare the documentation, and match the work to approved materials so projects clear without surprises.

### Do you take on small or self-managed Old Town associations?
Yes, converting self-managed buildings is one of the most common ways associations come to CenterPoint. We set up the books, vendor contracts, and governance calendar in a 30-to-60-day transition, with flat pricing from $20 per unit per month.

### Does CenterPoint manage associations in Old Town?
Yes. CenterPoint Association Management provides condominium, HOA, and townhome association management in Old Town, Chicago (ZIP 60610, 60614). Every association gets a dedicated manager, monthly financial reporting, and board support grounded in Illinois association law.

### How much does association management cost in Old Town?
Management starts at $20 per unit per month, quoted as a flat monthly fee based on your association's size, building systems, financial complexity, and service scope. It is never a percentage of your budget. See [pricing](https://www.centerpointmgmt.com/pricing) for what drives the fee.

### How does a Old Town association switch to CenterPoint?
Plan on a managed 30 to 60 day transition after your board gives notice under its current contract. We retrieve records from the outgoing manager, set up banking and vendor relationships, notify owners, and open board and resident access. ### How should a Old Town board compare management companies?
Compare at least three firms on the same terms: an active Illinois community association management firm license, a licensed manager, a flat monthly fee in writing, after-hours emergency coverage, and a written transition plan.
